comparisons.title: Added mass in the infinite-frequency limit: panel method against Capytaine on the same meshes
comparisons.reference: Capytaine 3.0.0, RadiationProblem with omega = inf, deep water
comparisons.quantity: Diagonal of the 6 × 6 added-mass matrix about the origin on the waterline (barge 20 × 8 m, 2 m draught, 768 panels; vertical cylinder D = 8 m, 40 m draught, 1128 panels; floating hemisphere a = 5 m, 2592 panels)
comparisons.validity: Translational terms within 3.4 % (largest: cylinder A11 surge), rotational terms within 5.7 % (largest: barge A44 roll), both codes on the identical flat-panel mesh.
comparisons.note: Both are constant-panel methods on the same triangles; the differences are discretisation differences between the potential formulation used here and Capytaine's default source formulation, not a converged reference. For the hemisphere the exact heave value is rho pi a^3 / 3 = 134172.18624706406 kg: the built-in result is the closer of the two. Terms that vanish by symmetry (hemisphere A44–A66, cylinder A66) are listed without a relative difference: both codes return discretisation noise there.

comparisons.title: Barge heave RAO in head seas: closed-form box model against Capytaine
comparisons.builtIn: boxBargeRAO({ L: 20, B: 8, T: 2, headingDeg: 180 }) — src/engine/hydro/floater.js
comparisons.quantity: heave amplitude per unit wave amplitude, barge 20 × 8 × 2 m draught
comparisons.validity: Within 5 % at wave periods 8, 10, 12, 14, 16, 20, 25 s (7 of 11); largest difference 31 % at T = 5 s.
comparisons.note: The closed-form model under-predicts heave in short waves: it is within 5 % from T = 8 s, twice its heave natural period 2 pi sqrt(2T/g) = 4.01 s (wavelength 100 m, five barge lengths), and 16 % low at 6 s (wavelength 56 m). It takes the heave added mass equal to the displacement (Capytaine: 1.47 times at 5 s, 2.69 times at 25 s) and a two-dimensional sectional damping. Reference: Capytaine coefficients read with readCapytaineCsv and solved with raoSolve for a mass of rho L B T, centre of gravity on the waterline, GMt = 1.667 m, GMl = 15.667 m, dry gyradii 0.35 B (roll) and 0.25 L (pitch). Deep water, zero speed.

comparisons.title: Barge pitch RAO in head seas: closed-form box model against Capytaine
comparisons.builtIn: boxBargeRAO({ L: 20, B: 8, T: 2, headingDeg: 180 }) — src/engine/hydro/floater.js
comparisons.quantity: pitch amplitude per unit wave amplitude, barge 20 × 8 × 2 m draught
comparisons.validity: Within 5 % at wave periods 6, 7, 8, 10, 12, 14, 16, 20, 25 s (9 of 11); largest difference 63 % at T = 4 s.
comparisons.note: The closed-form pitch is within 4 % from T = 6 s (wavelength 56 m, 2.8 barge lengths) and far too low at 4 s, where the wavelength (25 m) is close to the barge length. Reference: Capytaine coefficients read with readCapytaineCsv and solved with raoSolve for a mass of rho L B T, centre of gravity on the waterline, GMt = 1.667 m, GMl = 15.667 m, dry gyradii 0.35 B (roll) and 0.25 L (pitch). Deep water, zero speed.

comparisons.title: Barge heave RAO in beam seas: closed-form box model against Capytaine
comparisons.builtIn: boxBargeRAO({ L: 20, B: 8, T: 2, headingDeg: 90 }) — src/engine/hydro/floater.js
comparisons.quantity: heave amplitude per unit wave amplitude, barge 20 × 8 × 2 m draught
comparisons.validity: Within 5 % at wave periods 8, 10, 12, 14, 16, 20, 25 s (7 of 11); largest difference 42 % at T = 4 s.
comparisons.note: The heave force is the integral of the undisturbed pressure over the bottom, rho g L B exp(-kT) sinc(k_x L/2) sinc(k_y B/2), at every heading (the published closed form approximates the depth decay by exp(-|k cos beta| T), which in beam seas gave 1 + kT in long waves: +8 % at 10 s). The model now tends to 1 as Capytaine does (−0.81 % at 10 s) and is within 5 % from T = 8 s, twice its heave natural period of 4.01 s. Below that it is low (15 % at 6 s, 42 % at 4 s) for the reason given for head seas: added mass equal to the displacement and a two-dimensional sectional damping, 2.4 times the Capytaine value at 5 s for this barge of L/B = 2.5. Reference: Capytaine coefficients read with readCapytaineCsv and solved with raoSolve for a mass of rho L B T, centre of gravity on the waterline, GMt = 1.667 m, GMl = 15.667 m, dry gyradii 0.35 B (roll) and 0.25 L (pitch). Deep water, zero speed.

comparisons.title: Barge roll RAO in beam seas: one-degree-of-freedom model against Capytaine
comparisons.builtIn: boxBargeRAO({ L: 20, B: 8, T: 2, headingDeg: 90, GMt: 1.667, kxxDry: 0.35 B }) — src/engine/hydro/floater.js
comparisons.quantity: roll amplitude per unit wave amplitude, barge 20 × 8 × 2 m draught
comparisons.validity: Within 5 % at wave periods 7, 8, 10, 12, 14, 16, 20, 25 s (8 of 11); largest difference 15 % at T = 4 s.
comparisons.note: Model: Froude–Krylov moment plus relative-motion diffraction, strip added inertia of the rectangular section from DNV-RP-C205 Table D-1 (1237000 kg·m²; Capytaine 1136000 at infinite frequency, 1142000 at 5 s), radiation damping from the Haskind relation (51800 N·m·s at 5 s; Capytaine B44 51700), dry gyradius 0.35 B as in the reference and 5 % of critical added damping, 451800 N·m·s, which was also added to the Capytaine solution. The roll natural period is 5.3 s against 5.23 s with the Capytaine added inertia (the strip value has no end effect), which is what separates the two between 4 and 6 s; from 7 s the model is 1.8 %–4.8 % high. The reference itself is uncertain by a similar amount: its sway–roll added-mass terms are not symmetric on this mesh (A24 = -10700, A42 = -27200 kg·m at 25 s), and using A24 on both sides raises the reference roll by 3.1 %–5.4 % at 7–25 s. The model has no sway–roll coupling. Reference: Capytaine coefficients read with readCapytaineCsv and solved with raoSolve for a mass of rho L B T, centre of gravity on the waterline, GMt = 1.667 m, GMl = 15.667 m, dry gyradii 0.35 B (roll) and 0.25 L (pitch). Deep water, zero speed.

comparisons.title: Spar surge excitation force: slender-member model against Capytaine
comparisons.builtIn: buildFloater({ end1: 'hemisphere', free1: true }) + floaterRAO({ headingDeg: 0, viscous: false }) — src/engine/hydro/floater.js
comparisons.quantity: surge excitation force amplitude per unit wave amplitude, vertical cylinder D = 8 m, draught 40 m
comparisons.validity: Within 5 % at wave periods 6, 7, 8, 10, 12, 14, 16, 20, 25 s (9 of 11); largest difference 47 % at T = 4 s.
comparisons.note: Long-wave inertia force; diffraction reduces the true force in short waves (+6.4 % at 5 s, +47 % at 4 s, below the stated limit). Slender-member model: one vertical cylinder D = 8 m, draught 40 m, Ca = 1, hemisphere end added mass (137400 kg) and free-end loss of transverse added mass at the keel (DNV-RP-C205 Table D-2), radiation damping from the Haskind relation, no added damping, no drag. Reference: Capytaine coefficients solved with raoSolve using the mass and hydrostatic matrices of the same model and no added damping; its mesh is a 24-sided prism whose waterplane area is 1.1 % below that of the circle. The model states its own limit D/wavelength < 0.2, i.e. T > 5.06 s.

comparisons.title: Spar heave excitation force: slender-member model against Capytaine
comparisons.builtIn: buildFloater({ end1: 'hemisphere', free1: true }) + floaterRAO({ headingDeg: 0, viscous: false }) — src/engine/hydro/floater.js
comparisons.quantity: heave excitation force amplitude per unit wave amplitude, vertical cylinder D = 8 m, draught 40 m
comparisons.validity: Within 5 % at wave periods 5, 6, 7, 8, 10, 12, 14, 16, 20, 25 s (10 of 11); largest difference 34 % at T = 4 s.
comparisons.note: The heave force is the small difference between the pressure on the bottom and the inertia of the water below it, (rho g A − omega² m_a) exp(−kT). Two things separated the model from Capytaine before (+7.2 % at 10 s, +24 % at 7 s, wrong below). The wave kinematics were sampled at the centres of the 12 strips, which misses (k dl)²/24 of rho g A (1 − exp(−kT)), as large as the force itself in short waves; they are now integrated exactly along each strip, which alone leaves +6.8 % at 10 s and +14 % at 7 s. The rest was the end added mass: 'half-disc' gives 87470 kg, 'hemisphere' 137400 kg, Capytaine 134600 kg at 10 s; with the hemisphere the force is within 3.1 % from 5 s. At 4 s both forces are below 10 N/m, a hundred-thousandth of the long-wave value. Slender-member model: one vertical cylinder D = 8 m, draught 40 m, Ca = 1, hemisphere end added mass (137400 kg) and free-end loss of transverse added mass at the keel (DNV-RP-C205 Table D-2), radiation damping from the Haskind relation, no added damping, no drag. Reference: Capytaine coefficients solved with raoSolve using the mass and hydrostatic matrices of the same model and no added damping; its mesh is a 24-sided prism whose waterplane area is 1.1 % below that of the circle. The model states its own limit D/wavelength < 0.2, i.e. T > 5.06 s.

comparisons.title: Spar surge RAO: slender-member model against Capytaine
comparisons.builtIn: buildFloater({ end1: 'hemisphere', free1: true }) + floaterRAO({ headingDeg: 0, viscous: false }) — src/engine/hydro/floater.js
comparisons.quantity: surge amplitude per unit wave amplitude, vertical cylinder D = 8 m, draught 40 m
comparisons.validity: Within 5 % at wave periods 5, 6, 7, 8, 10, 12, 25 s (7 of 11); largest difference 24 % at T = 16 s.
comparisons.note: Surge couples with pitch, whose resonance lies at 14.8 s in the model and 14.63 s in the reference. Both solutions carry radiation damping only (model B55 −3.4 % from Capytaine at 14 s), so the peak is narrow and at 14, 16 and 20 s the difference (−17 %, +24 %, −9.4 %) follows the 1.2 % difference in natural period; at 20 s the surge RAO passes through a minimum of 0.25 m/m. Without the free-end loss the strip pitch added inertia is 14 % above Capytaine (with it 2 %), the resonance lies at 15.1 s and the differences at 14 and 16 s are −36 % and +84 %. Slender-member model: one vertical cylinder D = 8 m, draught 40 m, Ca = 1, hemisphere end added mass (137400 kg) and free-end loss of transverse added mass at the keel (DNV-RP-C205 Table D-2), radiation damping from the Haskind relation, no added damping, no drag. Reference: Capytaine coefficients solved with raoSolve using the mass and hydrostatic matrices of the same model and no added damping; its mesh is a 24-sided prism whose waterplane area is 1.1 % below that of the circle. The model states its own limit D/wavelength < 0.2, i.e. T > 5.06 s.

comparisons.title: NEMOH against Capytaine for the same exported barge, both read back by the application
comparisons.builtIn: readNemohResults on NEMOH v3 (master dcc8113, 2026-06-24) output — src/interop/nemoh.js
comparisons.quantity: Added mass, radiation damping and complex excitation force (exp(+i omega t), unit amplitude) of the barge 20 × 8 × 2 m, 768 panels, 5 frequencies
comparisons.unit: kg, kg·m² / N·s/m, N·m·s / N/m, N·m/m
comparisons.validity: Added mass within 0.048 %, damping within 0.092 % (largest: omega = 0.5 rad/s, B11), real and imaginary parts of the excitation within 0.22 % (largest: omega = 1 rad/s, heading 0, Re F5) for 0.25–1.25 rad/s.
comparisons.note: This is a solver-to-solver check of the hand-off itself: the same mesh went through the NEMOH writer and the Capytaine script, and two independent readers returned the same signs, units and phase convention. Parts of the excitation smaller than 2 % of the modulus are listed without a relative difference.

comparisons.title: Frame static deflection: beam elements against CalculiX
comparisons.reference: CalculiX 2.23, *STATIC, beams expanded to solid elements
comparisons.quantity: Nodal displacement under a point load; tube 500 × 20 mm or rectangle 200 × 400 mm, E = 210 GPa, 10 members per cantilever, 5 per portal member

cases.label: cantilever tube 10 m, tip load 10 kN: tip deflection uz (B32R, PIPE)
cantilever rectangle 0.2 × 0.4 m, tip load 10 kN: tip deflection uz (B31)
cantilever rectangle 0.2 × 0.4 m, tip load 10 kN: tip deflection uz (B32)
portal frame 6 × 5 m, 100 kN at the eaves: sway ux (B32R, PIPE)

comparisons.validity: All four deflections within 7.5 % (largest: portal frame 6 × 5 m, 100 kN at the eaves: sway ux (B32R, PIPE)).
comparisons.note: CalculiX has no beam element of its own: it expands each beam into 20-node bricks, which makes the tube slightly stiffer than Timoshenko beam theory. The built-in cantilever results equal P L^3 / (3 E I) + P L / (kappa G A). In the portal frame the expanded members overlap at the corners and form stiff joints of the size of the tube (0.5 m on members of 5 and 6 m), which the centre-line beam model does not have: the built-in sway is the larger.

comparisons.title: Natural frequencies of the cantilever tube 10 m: frame modal analysis against CalculiX
comparisons.quantity: First six natural frequencies, tube 500 × 20 mm, steel 7850 kg/m³, fixed bases
comparisons.validity: All six frequencies within 1.9 % (largest: cantilever tube 10 m, mode 6).
comparisons.note: Modes 1–4 are the two bending pairs, mode 5 is torsion, mode 6 the third bending mode; the built-in model is the softer of the two in bending, consistent with the static comparison.

comparisons.title: Natural frequencies of the portal frame 6 × 5 m: frame modal analysis against CalculiX
comparisons.quantity: First six natural frequencies, tube 500 × 20 mm, steel 7850 kg/m³, fixed bases
comparisons.validity: All six frequencies within 3.5 % (largest: portal frame 6 × 5 m, mode 6).
comparisons.note: In-plane sway, out-of-plane and beam modes in ascending order; the modes were matched by order.

comparisons.title: Elastic buckling factors of the cantilever tube 10 m: frame buckling analysis against CalculiX
comparisons.quantity: Load factors on 1 MN axial compression at the tip
comparisons.validity: All four factors within 1.5 % (largest: cantilever tube 10 m, mode 3).
comparisons.note: Euler: pi^2 E I / (4 L^2) / 1 MN = 4.508 for the first pair. The built-in factors are lower (it includes shear flexibility; the expanded solid tube of CalculiX is stiffer in bending).

comparisons.title: Elastic buckling factors of the portal frame 6 × 5 m: frame buckling analysis against CalculiX
comparisons.quantity: Load factors on 1 MN on each column top
comparisons.validity: All four factors within 5.6 % (largest: portal frame 6 × 5 m, mode 3).
comparisons.note: Sway buckling first; the modes were matched by order.

comparisons.title: Simply supported plate under uniform pressure: Navier series against CalculiX shells
comparisons.quantity: Centre deflection of a 2 × 1.5 m plate, t = 20 mm, 10 kPa

cases.label: centre deflection, S6 shells (default of the writer)

comparisons.validity: Within 0.66 % of CalculiX S6 shells; CalculiX S3 shells give 0.116 of the plate-theory deflection and are not a usable reference.
comparisons.note: The S3 result is a property of CalculiX (three-node shells are expanded into six-node wedges that lock in bending), not of the plate theory; the writer therefore uses S6 unless elementOrder 1 is requested. Thin-plate theory has no shear deformation.
